summary.intent: Implement GitHub issue #618 (cipher-box core: strict deterministic-CBOR codec, error surface, and KAT test vectors) while orchestrating parallel worktree agents for issues #624 (API auth), #623 (engine scaffold), and #645 (Tauri desktop shell), then run a crypto/security review on the resulting PR.
summary.outcome: PR #659 for #618 was opened, reviewed (standards + spec sub-agents), hardened, and merged-check-registered as a required CI gate; #624 and #645 finished cleanly in separate worktrees awaiting human review; a /crypto-privacy-review pass on PR #659 found and fixed 3 real issues (error Display truncation, missing encode-side depth guard, CI freshness gate blind to untracked files) plus 3 more from CodeRabbit/Greptile threads, and the crypto-privacy-review skill's own output contract was corrected to stop writing security reports into the repo/PR branch.

repo: cipher-box crates/core must stay free of I/O/clock/RNG per blueprint doctrine; kat_gen.rs is an example binary so file I/O there is acceptable, unlike in src/

KAT vectors and manifest are meant to be generator-owned; kat_gen.rs originally preserved manifestVersion/profile/structureTags/kdfEdges from the existing file on disk, letting a hand-edit survive the CI freshness diff — fixed so the generator is the sole writer of every manifest byte
Half-float bit pattern f90014 aliases the CBOR simple-value encoding for `false` — decode dispatch must key off additional-info, not just the byte value, or this class of bug slips through
proptest's `fork` feature (via wait-timeout) does not compile under wasm32-wasip1; the dev-dependency must be split per-target (forkless config for wasm)

The `rust` CI path filter didn't include .cargo/config.toml, so changes to the wasmtime runner config could skip the core-kats job entirely — testing.md's gate-must-fire-on-input-change rule requires it be added

Trust vs malformed error classification (e.g. indefinite-length = trust, tags/floats/oversize-simple-values = malformed) is not directly derivable from blueprint/core.md and needed explicit documented rationale in error.rs since KAT vectors freeze the classification (re-classing later breaks vectors)
#645 (Tauri shell) had to exclude cipherbox-desktop from the three existing workspace cargo CI jobs so non-desktop PRs don't pay the webkit/tauri build cost

.claude/commands/crypto-privacy-review.md is repo-tracked and originally instructed writing reports to .planning/security/ inside the repo — this causes review reports to get committed onto feature branches, which is wrong; it was edited to output to a scratchpad location instead

code.finding: rust path filter was missing .cargo/config.toml, letting wasmtime runner config changes skip the core-kats gate; fixed by standards-review agent's finding

build_manifest previously preserved manifestVersion/profile/structureTags/kdfEdges from the existing file rather than generating them, undermining the 'committed generator is sole writer' guarantee; fixed to hardcode/own these fields

trust/malformed classification boundary needed an explicit documented rationale comment since it's a judgment call not derivable from the blueprint, and Display formatting had a truncation issue flagged by the crypto-privacy-review as potentially leaking info
encoder lacked the MAX_DEPTH guard the decoder enforced — crypto-privacy-review flagged this asymmetry as fix #2
final review-feedback fix applied here after CodeRabbit/Greptile pass on PR #659 (specific content not detailed in transcript)

workflow: Effective pattern: launch independent, dependency-free issues as background worktree agents (via Agent tool with isolation) while continuing interactive work on the current issue in the main session, then verify each agent's on-disk branch/commits before trusting its self-report
Before starting parallel work, explicitly check open issues' 'Depends on:' lines to find truly independent slices safe to run concurrently
After sub-agents finish, run the full verification battery yourself (native + wasm tests, clippy, fmt, generator freshness) rather than trusting agent reports alone
Use two independent review agents (standards-review and spec-review) on a diff before opening a PR, then fix actionable findings and document accepted judgment calls in the PR body
Register the new CI job name as a required branch-protection check only after a PR run proves the job name, not before

friction: GitHub branch protection required-check registration needed checking both classic and new-style protection rules to find where to register the job
wasm32-wasip1 test target broke on proptest's fork/wait-timeout dependency, requiring a target-specific Cargo.toml dev-dependency split

The crypto-privacy-review skill's default output path (.planning/security/ in-repo) caused a review report to get committed onto the PR branch by mistake, requiring the commit to be dropped and the skill file itself patched

CodeRabbit/Greptile review threads on PR #659 surfaced additional real findings (order-fragile absent-checks assertion in kat_gen) after the crypto-privacy-review pass, requiring another round of fixes and a force-push
